text:
Maria: Heads-up — after rolling kv-page refactor to canary tonight, prod shows steady memory creep on long contexts (~5k tokens). Repro with convo replay. :eyes:
Ryan: Which canary? I saw the rollout note: canary-evict-v2. Ring?
Maria: canary-evict-v2 in us-west, 3 instances. Heap grows ~200MB/min on long seqs. pprof shows a lot of slab allocations in kv-fragment pool.
Ben: ran a local repro loop and I see fragments whose index offsets don't match token positions — looks like misaligned indices after eviction.
Alice: Can you share a tiny repro?
Ben: gist of the loop:
```python
# minimal loop
for _ in range(500):
  client.generate(prompt=long_prompt, stream=False)
```
Ben: after ~200 loops GC doesn't free slabs; looked at logs and `kv_page->base_offset` sometimes lags the real token index by exactly 64 tokens.
Maria: Log snippet shows: "evict shard 3: keep_offset 10240 -> 10176 (delta -64)" — that -64 stands out.
Ryan: hmm, maybe rounding when we align pages to cache_line*4 after the refactor. I changed align_to math in the eviction path.
Ben: dug into the write path: eviction runs async, and new fragment allocation race uses a stale request_id if the eviction callback races with the writer. That can produce cross-request contamination.
Alice: Ugh. Do we have a quick mitigation? Disable reuse of freed fragment slots? Increase alignment to avoid -64?
Maria: I'm rolling a rollback to previous eviction heuristic now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollback canary-evict-v2 -> previous (us-west, 3 instances) :shipit:
Ben: diagnostics to run on a repro node:
```
grep 'evict shard' /var/log/kv/*.log | sed -n '1,200p'
```
Ryan: I opened PR #4281: capture request_id earlier, push it into the eviction callback closure, and add an assert that fragment.tag == current_request_tag before reuse. Also added a guard against negative delta.
Alice: Can we add a unit+stress test that simulates concurrent eviction+write with randomized alignment boundaries? That will catch this flake.
Ben: added a test harness in the PR and a temporary canary config where align_to=128; that avoids the exact -64 drift.
Maria: After rollback, mem growth stopped on canary. Soak run continuing for 30m.
Ryan: Follow-ups: add fragment_stale_count metric, capture first_token_index in traces, and audit all alignment math (floor vs trunc).
Alice: I'll own the postmortem and timeline once we confirm root cause.
Maria: Thanks all — if PR CI is green let's merge and stage a slow rollout. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollback complete on 3 instances in us-west (1968000275)
